problem_markdown: A walk starts at vertex $A$ of a regular octagon and at each step moves to an adjacent vertex, stopping at its first visit to the opposite vertex $E$. If $a_n$ counts walks stopping after exactly $n$ steps, prove $a_{2n-1}=0$ and $a_{2n}=((2+\sqrt2)^{n-1}-(2-\sqrt2)^{n-1})/\sqrt2$.
solutions_markdown:
Parity of distance to $E$ changes at every step, so odd stopping times are impossible. Put $A_n=a_{2n}$ and let $B_n$ count walks stopping at $E$ after $2n$ steps when starting two edges from $E$. Looking at the first two moves gives, for $n\ge2$,
$$A_n=2A_{n-1}+2B_{n-1},\qquad B_n=A_{n-1}+2B_{n-1}.$$
Here paths reaching $E$ during those first two moves contribute only when $n=1$, and are excluded for $n\ge2$. Initially $A_1=0,B_1=1$, so $A_2=2$. Eliminating $B$ yields $A_n=4A_{n-1}-2A_{n-2}$ for $n\ge3$. The two characteristic roots are $2\pm\sqrt2$; the initial values give
$$A_n=\frac{(2+\sqrt2)^{n-1}-(2-\sqrt2)^{n-1}}{\sqrt2},$$
as required.
